reverse-text.assumptionNote: Characters are reversed by Unicode code point, so emoji and combined marks stay intact as far as the browser's string handling allows.
benefits: Three reversal modes: characters, word order, or each line separately.
Instant results — no button to press, updates as you type.
Fun for puzzles, palindromes and playful messages.
Copy or download the reversed text with one click.
Private — your text never leaves your browser.

faqs.a: Character mode reverses every character including spaces. Word mode reverses the order of words but keeps each word readable. Line mode reverses the characters inside each line separately.
faqs.q: What is the difference between the three modes?

faqs.a: Use Word order mode. It keeps each word intact and only flips their sequence.
faqs.q: How do I reverse the order of words?

faqs.a: Yes — the tool is fully reversible. Reversing the output with the same mode returns the original text.
faqs.q: Can I get the original text back?

faqs.a: Yes. Characters are handled by Unicode code point, so emoji and Hindi/Arabic text reverse correctly.
Try reversing your text and comparing — a palindrome reads the same forwards and backwards in Character mode.
faqs.q: Can I use this to check palindromes?

faqs.a: Yes — everything runs locally in your browser.

reverse-text.formula:
chars:  reverse of the character sequence
words:  reverse of the word sequence (spaces preserved)
lines:  each line's characters reversed independently
howTo: Type or paste your text into the input box.
Pick a mode: Characters, Word order, or Each line.
Read the reversed text from the output box as you type.
Copy it to the clipboard or download it as a .txt file.
Try Word order mode for readable-but-backwards sentences.
keyFacts: Character mode reverses the entire text, spaces included.
Word order mode keeps every word readable and only flips their sequence.
Line mode reverses the characters within each line separately.
Reversing is fully reversible — run it again to get the original.
Everything is computed locally in your browser.

limitations: Reversing is not encryption — anyone can reverse it back.

Word mode treats punctuation attached to words as part of the word.
